alpha: RGBA, alpha range 0–255; original generated alpha preserved without pixel editing
layout: Eight independent cels in four columns and two rows, read left to right then top to bottom
integration_note: Use individual silhouette bounds, not equal-grid crop. Full thrusts extend past nominal quarter-grid lines but remain separated from adjacent characters. walk.review: Eight separate bodies; contact, lowered weight, passing and lifted-stride poses; same armor, shield and complete spear in all eight.
walk.initial_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production sprite animation sheet for the existing Sengoku side-scrolling beat-em-up game. Reference image is the exact character identity and armor/weapon design reference, not an output layout to preserve. Create ONE new independent animation sheet of ASAKURA KAGETSUNE, the same Japanese adult male warrior seen in the reference: black iron lamellar and plate armor with narrow old-gold trim, charcoal padded trousers, deep forest-green waist wraps and hanging green skirt panels/scarf, black kabuto with small gold crest, armored shin guards and straw/leather sandals; right hand carries the same long straight dark wooden yari with narrow silver leaf-shaped spearhead and small green tassel, left forearm carries the same narrow tall rectangular dark wooden shield with antique brass edging and central round boss. Realistic finely painted 2.5D sprite art identical to the reference, anatomically correct, detailed metal, cloth and wood; no chibi, no pixel art, no generic 3D toy.
OUTPUT: largest supported high-resolution wide LANDSCAPE canvas, target 3840x2160. Exactly EIGHT complete full-body character cels in a strict uniform 4-column x 2-row grid, reading left to right then top to bottom. Invisible grid, NO lines, no letters, numbers, labels, text or borders. TRUE transparent background, alpha zero outside the eight character silhouettes. No brown/gray background, no checkerboard, no ground, no cast shadows, no glow, no smoke, no VFX.
Every cel is separately centered in its own equal cell. Whole warrior INCLUDING BOTH FEET, BOTH HANDS, ENTIRE SHIELD, EVERY PART OF THE SPEAR must fit completely inside its cell. Large clear transparent gutters: no body, tassel, weapon or shield may touch or enter another cell. Keep body scale consistent across all 8 cels and fixed camera at right-facing three-quarter game angle. Keep virtual ground baseline identical within each row and planted foot contact believable. When extending the spear, leave enough width by keeping each full silhouette safely within 80% of its cell. Exactly one head, one torso, two arms, two legs, one shield and one complete spear per cel. Distinct anatomically continuous motion, not scaled/rotated copies of a standing pose.
Animation: an 8-frame LOOPING WALK CYCLE, warrior steadily walking toward screen-right in a guarded patrol stance; shield always on left forearm in front of torso, spear safely carried diagonally upward-right (not changing weapon length). Cel 1 left-foot contact forward/right foot back; cel 2 lower weight onto left foot, trailing right heel lifting; cel 3 right leg passes under hips, shield bobs subtly; cel 4 right knee swings forward and left heel lifts; cel 5 right-foot contact forward/left foot back, mirror gait phase of cel1 but SAME rightward facing identity; cel 6 settle onto right foot with trailing left heel lift; cel 7 left leg passes under hips; cel 8 left knee swings forward approaching cel1. Clear alternating leg positions and knee flexion, tiny natural shoulder/cloth follow-through, no attack, no running and no rigid sliding. Frames 1 through8 must form a smooth continuous gait loop, never turn to face the camera.
walk.repair_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. EDIT the supplied animation sheet while preserving this same Asakura Kagetsune face, black and old-gold armor, green sashes, rectangular dark wood brass-edged shield and full dark-wood yari with silver leaf blade and green tassel, the same realistic painted style.
Repair the production sprite layout. Exactly 8 isolated COMPLETE character cels in 4 columns x 2 rows, rightward-facing game camera, on TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha. Highest supported landscape resolution, target 3840x2160. Every cel must fit inside its own cell with large transparent space around it. Make the figures INTENTIONALLY SMALL on the canvas: head-to-feet BODY HEIGHT only 40% of the cell height, full silhouette INCLUDING weapons no more than 75% of cell width and 75% of cell height. This smaller scale is essential: the previous large poses ran spears through adjacent cels. Do NOT enlarge characters to fill the grid. Eight compact sprites with extensive empty transparent gutters is the intended final appearance. Keep identical body scale between poses and per-row foot baselines at 85% of cell height. No pixel or part of a sprite may cross a cell boundary or overlap another sprite. No labels, grid lines, background, smoke, glow, shadows or VFX.
In EVERY pose visibly retain BOTH hands, BOTH legs and feet, the ONE shield strapped to the LEFT forearm, and the COMPLETE long spear in the RIGHT hand. Never omit the spear during defense. A braced spear should angle upward/backward so its full shaft and blade remain visible above/beside the shield. Never omit the shield during a thrust; show it on the other forearm against the chest. Keep weapons anatomically attached and natural, no detached spare weapons.
Also REPAIR the gait: the current sheet mostly repeats one stride phase. Create an actual 8-step LOOP: 1 nearer LEFT leg fully forward in contact/far RIGHT back; 2 lower on left with right heel lifted; 3 RIGHT passing with both legs nearly aligned beneath hips and right knee visibly bent; 4 RIGHT swinging clearly forward while left toes push off; 5 far RIGHT leg fully forward in contact/near LEFT back, visibly opposite to frame1; 6 lower on right with left heel lifted; 7 LEFT passing with legs nearly aligned under hips and left knee bent; 8 LEFT swings forward toward pose1. Never flip the whole character or change facing. Spear carried diagonally upward-right, left-forearm shield forward; arms/cloth bob gently. The difference between LEFT-LEADING and RIGHT-LEADING strides must be unambiguous, not 8 copies of one same-leg stride.
